summary: Hold — unresolved. Innomet has genuine specialty-powder and tungsten-heavy-alloy capabilities, customer qualification and export momentum. sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Hold — unresolved. Innomet has genuine specialty-powder and tungsten-heavy-alloy capabilities, customer qualification and export momentum. These have not yet established durable excess returns. FY26 sales rose 65.6% while PAT fell 15.7%; deposit release inflated reported operating cash. Material historical corrections remain incompletely reconciled, and the new subsidiary’s claims and funding are unverified. At ₹281.25 the market prices a demanding ramp. BQS, GQS and IAS are NS, not zero or neutral. All ordinary investment returns and entry prices are withheld. This is a capacity-monetisation and strategic-materials growth option, not an evidence-backed compounder. Qualified manufacturing know-how is the strongest asset. The decisive weakness is that growth, accounting reliability, operating cash and attributable incremental returns do not yet align. A lower quote cannot itself resolve the financial-reliability and funding gates. The positive case becomes stronger if corrections are fully reconciled and qualified capacity produces repeatable cash after working capital, necessary capex and dilution.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
The exact issuer is Innomet Advanced Materials Limited, formerly Innomet Advanced Materials Private Limited, NSE Emerge INNOMET, ISIN INE0S1D01010, CIN L27101TG2019PLC132262. The information cutoff is 20 October 2026, Asia/Kolkata. The official 19 October close is ₹281.25, distinct from the ₹283 last trade. The August allotment increased issued shares from 12,940,138 to 13,390,138, implying market capitalization of ₹376.5976 crore. The dated exchange master retains the earlier share count and is not used as the economic denominator.

FY26 financials are standalone because Swastik was not a subsidiary at 31 March. The 57.5% acquisition became effective on 25 September. This is a subsequent perimeter change, not an FY26 non-consolidation error. The accounts use Indian GAAP Accounting Standards under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, not Ind AS. Forecasts are parent-only until subsidiary opening accounts are available; no separate subsidiary value is added. The five-year investor horizon is 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031. The 15% nominal pretax equity hurdle is an analytical assumption, separate from the DCF discount-rate sensitivity. The ₹5 lakh reference position is illustrative, not suitability advice.

Confidence is high for identity, official price, allotment and acquisition dates; medium for the extracted reported financial figures and attributed product mix; low for comparable history, incremental returns and current group financeability. Gates are G1 Conditional, G2 Hold, G3 Hold and G4 Conditional.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
The 13 factor assessments are GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV NS, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH 3, BAL NS, EXEC 4, EARN 3, R NS, D NS, P 2 and L 8. BQS has a known contribution of 3.22 at 68% coverage, with a mathematical missing-score bound of 3.54–6.42. GQS has 1.95 at 45% coverage and an uncapped bound of 2.50–7.45. CASH 3 caps a computable GQS at 5, giving a capped bound of 2.50–5.00; it does not turn an unknown score into 5. IAS has 1.00 at 20% coverage and a bound of 1.80–9.00. Its Q input is the missing final BQS, not a fabricated average.

All three aggregates remain NS and are excluded from numerical rankings. Exact Decimal weights and contributions are retained. No severe-governance override is applied. G2 prevents a favorable investment classification. Moving GOV or MOAT by one point changes the known BQS component by 0.20 each; moving DUR or EARN by one changes GQS by 0.20 or 0.15. These are judgment sensitivities, not statistical confidence intervals, and missing factors are never renormalized away.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Innomet sells atomised metal and alloy powders and tungsten-heavy-alloy shapes/components manufactured through powder metallurgy and sintering. Its economics combine material procurement, process yield, technical service and qualification, followed by collection on orders. This is not recurring subscription revenue. FY26 management-reported mix was approximately ₹40.6 crore powders, or 75.4%, and ₹13.3 crore THA, or 24.6%. Rounded divisional totals differ slightly from audited revenue of ₹53.8641 crore. Audited export earnings were ₹9.8281 crore. General industrial powders remain the majority: treating all revenue as aerospace or defence would overstate the mix.

Customers require chemistry, particle distribution, density, dimensional tolerance and traceability. A certification permits consideration; repeat orders and profitable output are separate tests. Current customer concentration, retention cohorts and segment capital/profits are not disclosed sufficiently for attribution. Swastik adds a restart/backward-integration project, not a purchased established profit stream: disclosed turnover was nil while operations were halted.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible moat is qualification friction. Customers must validate consistency, traceability and performance, making an established supplier less interchangeable than a commodity trader. Repeated industrial orders and reported ISO 9001/AS9100D systems support useful differentiation, not monopoly or demonstrated pricing power. The prospectus describes nonexclusive customer relationships that generally lack long-term agreements. FY26 operating EBITDA margin fell from approximately 15.6% to 10.4% despite greater THA and export mix. Raw-metal inflation, development and selling costs can overwhelm mix benefits.

Independent economic comparators are Höganäs for broad powder capability and customer engineering, Pometon for ferrous/nonferrous and specialty powders, and Kennametal Densalloy for THA balance, damping and shielding applications. Their primary catalogues demonstrate technical alternatives. They are not clean same-scale quoted valuation peers; no unsupported financial ranking or peer-multiple average is assigned. Swastik is a distressed acquired asset, not a successful independent comparator. A MOAT score above the middle range would require persistent premium margins, multiyear retention, price/volume evidence and realized returns on incremental capital.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The historical table separates original and later comparative presentations. Prospectus revenue for FY21/FY22/FY23/FY24 was ₹12.4378/22.3842/27.1293/28.9919 crore. FY25 accounts restated FY24 revenue to ₹24.8958 crore because output GST had previously been included in sales and other expenses. FY25 and FY26 report ₹32.5248 and ₹53.8641 crore. Corrected FY24–FY26 two-year revenue CAGR is 47.09%, with absolute additions of ₹7.6290 crore and ₹21.3393 crore.

That two-year result is not a verified three- or five-year organic CAGR. The earlier GST-net bridge and current price/volume decomposition are unavailable, so REV remains NS rather than receiving a high score from mixed gross/net history. FY26 growth of 65.61% includes genuine demand and exports according to management, but the contribution of metal-price inflation is not quantified. H1 FY26 presentation figures of ₹23.53 crore sales and ₹2.02 crore PAT imply balancing H2 revenue of approximately ₹30.3341 crore and PAT of −₹0.4473 crore, affected by reversals. No H1 FY27 result was verified by the cutoff, and a seasonal half-year is not annualized into a supposed current TTM.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Nameplate capacity is not output. The prospectus reports water-atomised sales of 190.378, 193.472 and 201.589 tonnes in FY22–FY24 against 600 TPA: approximately 31.73%, 32.25% and 33.60% utilization. June 2026 management describes a 40–42 tonne monthly run rate against 50 tonnes monthly capacity, or 80–84%, and THA at approximately 50% of a new 5-tonne monthly capacity. Neither is an audited FY26 annual utilization rate. The water roadmap of 1,200 TPA, commercial gas target of 150 TPA and DRDO-supported 100 kg atomiser/200–250 TPA project are separate stages. The ₹8.73 crore sanctioned project outlay is not unrestricted cash. Swastik’s attributed installed capacity requires refurbishment, restart and customer acceptance.

The model converts sales and mix into illustrative powder/THA tonnage, provides capacity capex above the installed 600/60 TPA baseline, and includes maintenance capex of 4% of sales plus cash working capital. Assumed realizations and marginal capacity costs are stressed, not presented as demonstrated unit returns. FY26 ROIC of approximately 4.20% and an incremental book proxy of −3.16% are diagnostics only. Corrections, long contract advances and ramp timing prevent an attributable capital-return bridge. Thus CAP is NS rather than a score inferred from current ROCE, nameplate expansion or a large addressable market.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Family control, disclosed commercial related-party transactions and director loans do not by themselves imply misconduct. FY26 executive director pay of ₹0.45 crore was approximately 28.6% of PAT; an additional director salary of ₹0.1453 crore also matters. Prasad purchases of ₹0.4815 crore and Keerthi capital purchases of ₹0.3934 crore need commercial benchmarking. AGM related-party ceilings of ₹6 crore for Keerthi and ₹50 crore for Swastik are material relative to earnings. Voting results establish approval, not actual cash drawdown or misuse.

The 18 August allotment of 450,000 shares at ₹131 raised ₹5.895 crore. A 25% deposit on 500,000 promoter warrants at ₹131 added ₹1.6375 crore; the remaining ₹4.9125 crore is optional exercise cash. A further 1,192,200 warrants at ₹210 were approved in September, but allotment and receipt were not verified. Their full ₹25.0362 crore is not base-case funding. Full exercise would lift shares to 15,082,338; the additional 260,000-share ESOP limit produces a separate 15,342,338-share sensitivity, not an assertion of grants. Share-count expansion and ownership dilution are different measures.

Delivery is mixed. THA capacity reportedly increased from 18 to 60 TPA and export orders are tangible. June’s ₹35.99 crore order claim was expected to execute within H1, but actual completion was not verified by the cutoff. Swastik was described as effectively acquired in June, while the formal September filing establishes completion on 25 September. Gas-atomisation plans are not proof of accepted commercial output.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Four reconciliations are decisive. First, the FY25 opening-reserve correction of ₹4.1679 crore includes quantified depreciation of ₹0.2747 crore and inventory of ₹2.8669 crore, leaving ₹1.0263 crore unbridged. The company discloses historical asset-life/depreciation errors and inventory that included GST and used market value rather than lower cost/net realizable value. Second, the June 2026 CFO explains ₹1.92 crore development costs that could not be supported for capitalization to the auditor’s satisfaction and ₹2.96 crore technology-transfer revenue reversed because it did not materialize. Management says products have commercialized and the accounting method has not changed. The response is preserved; neither item is automatically added back to recurring profit.

Third, reported FY26 CFO of ₹9.2589 crore includes ₹8 crore deposit release and a −₹2.5551 crore borrowing movement. Removing both gives a classification sensitivity of ₹3.814 crore. FY25 becomes −₹13.303 crore after excluding deposit placement and borrowing inflow. FY24–FY26 adjusted cumulative CFO/PAT is approximately −1.44 times. Even an optimistic add-back of the entire ₹4.1679 crore prior correction leaves cumulative conversion negative. This is an analytical reclassification, not an auditor-certified corrected statement. The CFO’s explanation of fixed-deposit maturity is positive counterevidence, not evidence of recurring owner cash.

Fourth, long contract advances of ₹5.7053 crore and prepaids of ₹4.6785 crore require recoverability and contractual-term evidence. Receivables of ₹11.0028 crore imply 58.81 average days; ₹0.5913 crore is older than one year without allowance. Debt of ₹14.916 crore includes current maturities of ₹1.5683 crore. Cash is ₹2.7586 crore; a separate ₹0.1498 crore margin deposit is restricted. Bank guarantees of ₹0.1398 crore are contingent, not automatically debt. Current tax ₹0.4569 crore and statutory liabilities ₹0.3545 crore are paid once in the conditional opening bridge, distinct from future modeled tax. Gratuity, capital creditors and accrued interest are counted once. Audits are unmodified, bank returns reportedly agree with books and no default was reported. G2 Hold concerns specific unresolved reliability bridges, not an allegation of fraud.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹281.25 and 13,390,138 issued shares, historical cross-checks are 239.46 times FY26 PAT and 8.78 times March equity. March cash/debt imply 69.34 times EBITDA and 7.22 times sales, explicitly stale enterprise-value diagnostics. Current October group EV is not established. The primary method is linked annual operating cash/funding with terminal EV/EBITDA. DCF sensitivities use discount rates of 14/17/20%, terminal growth of 3/5% and terminal ROIC of 12/18%; they are cross-checks, not funded fair values.

Bear/base/bull FY27 sales are ₹60/78/95 crore, reaching FY32 sales of ₹77/178/310 crore. Terminal EBITDA margins are 10/17/21% and exit multiples 7/12/16 times. Even the base requires margin repair and sustained growth. The model separates March-to-18 August operations, a zero-day actual capital-receipt event, the remaining pre-entry period, the FY27 investor stub, FY28–FY31 and an exact-day FY32 stub through 20 October 2031. Opening tax and statutory balances are conservatively paid before the August event, not backfilled with later equity. The final fiscal denominator is 366 days. No cash flow after the investor terminal governs financeability.

All ordinary returns and entries are null, including downside rows. The model tests cash immediately before the actual 18 August capital receipt. All three paths breach the required cash floor before that receipt under the conservative opening-tax settlement assumption, so all non-rescue conditional returns are also null, including bear. This is not a finding of an actual historical cash shortfall or default. Rescue is separate, grossed up for fees and explicitly dilutive, never assumed available. Full annual ledgers and sensitivity rows are embedded. Required operating cash remains in terminal value and DCF reinvestment. IPO proceeds, grants, operating property and subsidiary value are not added again.

All non-rescue conditional annual returns are null after pre-entry cash-floor breaches. Base and bull peak non-rescue cash gaps are ₹7.4965 crore and ₹12.2292 crore. At a 50% equity discount and 3% fees, the counterfactual base rescue, including hypothetical pre-entry financing that is not established historical funding, raises ₹7.7284 crore gross, dilutes existing holders by 3.94% and gives a -2.92% annual return. Bull rescue returns 19.09%. None is an ordinary supported investment return. Hurdles of 12/15/18%, financing discounts of 25/50/70%, fees of 0/3/6% and execution costs of 0/1/3/5% each side are separate tests.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is that demand for strategic materials and technical qualification fail to produce attractive value added. Metal inflation or a large export order raises sales and inventory funding needs while repricing lags. Delayed customer acceptance lowers utilization; discounts or rejects erode contribution; receivables and specialized stock trap cash; development costs and furnaces still require spending. Existing bank and promoter funding needs renewal. Swastik introduces restart and residual-claim risk rather than instant cheap feedstock.

The linked stress combines working capital ten percentage points worse, margin four points lower, capex at 1.5 times, non-renewal of the ₹4.1198 crore working-capital line and an additional ₹1.5018 crore inaccessible to the parent. Subscription money may initially remain group cash, so this extra parent-only constraint is a sensitivity, not a duplicate baseline debit. A modeled shortfall is not a verified default. The separate lost-advance sensitivity assumes a new payment to replace productive contract advances. An impairment alone is noncash: the original advance is already paid and included in opening ONWC. Equity rescue can keep a business operating yet fail the 15% per-share hurdle. The thesis-break variable is collectible post-metal-cost cash per unit of capital, not headline orders. The market may already understand certification, exports and China+1; the differentiated question is whether those features can justify the cash economics implied by price.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold price gain over five years requires 37.97% annual compounding; tenfold requires 58.49%. At a 20-times terminal P/E with unchanged shares, 5× requires approximately ₹94.15 crore PAT and 10× approximately ₹188.30 crore, versus FY26 PAT of ₹1.5727 crore. A 10% net margin implies sales of about ₹941.5 crore or ₹1,883.0 crore before financing dilution. These are reverse requirements, not targets.

Qualified capacity, working capital, raw-material security, engineering yield and customer access would all require major advances. Multiple compression and new shares raise the burden. The modeled bull is already demanding and does not establish this scale or a financed path to it. Classification: Speculative / unsupported, not mathematically impossible. No success probability is assigned and no large-market narrative substitutes for attributable incremental returns.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Obtain the earlier GST-net history and complete ₹4.1679 crore reserve-adjustment bridge. The unexplained quantified residual is ₹1.0263 crore. Continued ambiguity keeps G2 on Hold; a coherent auditor-backed reconciliation improves confidence.
2. Track cash after proper financing/deposit classification. FY26 analytical CFO is ₹3.814 crore and the latest three-year sum is negative. Require cumulative cash after necessary capex and long advances, not repeated deposit release.
3. Monitor average receivable days of 58.81 and ₹0.5913 crore older than one year. Above 75 days or growing unprovided aged balances warrants review, not an automatic trade.
4. Track metal value added, yield and margins. FY26 operating EBITDA margin is 10.4%; the base assumes 14–17%. Continued sales growth with sub-10% margins and weak cash would undermine that path.
5. Reconcile opening orders plus wins less executions/cancellations. June ₹35.99 crore and August over ₹45 crore are attributed snapshots, not additive backlog. October Federal-Mogul consideration includes IGST, packing and freight, so it is not all net revenue.
6. Verify commissioning, accepted throughput and yields against 600 TPA water/60 TPA THA baseline rather than nameplate announcements.
7. Obtain Swastik opening net assets, liabilities, cash, restart plan and noncontrolling-interest allocation after 25 September before assigning profits or recovery value.
8. Track the 13,390,138 current shares, outstanding 500,000 promoter warrants, approved 1,192,200 further warrants, exercise receipts, fees, ESOP grants and actual related-party drawdowns.
9. Recheck the 600-share lot, ST series, current restrictions, spread and queues before implementation. Review on new financial and material filings; this is a research plan, not an automation or trade instruction.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved. The research priority is financial reconciliation and funded operating conversion, not an eligible investment recommendation. BQS, GQS and IAS are NS with coverage and bounds disclosed. The company cannot currently meet a compounder-candidate test while REV, CAP and BAL are missing, CASH is 3 and MOAT is 5. This is not an insolvency or severe-integrity classification.

A lower price would improve expectations but not repair G2 or G3. Price becomes decisive after reliable comparable accounts, current group claims and accessible resources, attributable capital returns and repeatable cash are established. New evidence should prompt a genuine rerun, not preservation of the Hold by habit. No personalized position size, purchase/sale instruction or promise of execution is made. A conditional rescue price is not an ordinary entry recommendation.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary exchange annual reports, the prospectus, allotment/acquisition filings, AGM voting results and official NSE archives support the record. Management calls and presentations are identified as attributed statements. Each material claim has evidence IDs, dates, locators and original-source URLs/hashes. Primary product catalogues establish technical alternatives, not peer financial superiority. The main open questions are the full historical correction bridge, earlier GST-net revenue, FY26 interim reversal reconciliation, long-advance/prepaid recoverability, subsidiary opening claims/restart cash and exact further-warrant status.

Private analytical backups exclude original PDFs, HTML, OCR, images and shareholder lists. They retain financial-only extracts, models, source references and calculation checks. Offline reproduction verifies arithmetic and internal consistency, not fresh authentication of original documents. The model assumes maintenance capex of 4% of sales, realization of ₹0.085 crore per powder tonne and ₹0.70 crore per THA tonne, incremental capacity costs, working capital of 43–60% of sales, 25% tax, 9% interest and a 3% operating cash reserve. These are hypotheses with sensitivities, not company commitments. No loss-year tax benefit is assumed. Terminal growth requires reinvestment and retained cash. Missing information is ND or NS, not zero.

reconciliations.subject: GST presentation
reconciliations.primary_explanation: FY25 audited P&L states output GST was included in previous revenue and other expenses and adjusts current/prior comparative. FY24 revenue changes from 28.9919 to 24.8958 crore.
reconciliations.unresolved: Reliable GST-net FY21-FY23 bridge not located. Do not calculate a scored organic three/five-year CAGR across the change.

reconciliations.subject: Opening reserves FY25
reconciliations.primary_explanation: Company acknowledges incorrect useful-life/depreciation calculation and inventory including GST or valued at market instead of lower of cost/NRV.
reconciliations.counterevidence: Corrections are disclosed and FY25/FY26 audit opinions are unmodified. No inference of fraud.

reconciliations.subject: FY26 interim reversals
reconciliations.status: Management explanation recorded; full audited line bridge unavailable
reconciliations.company_response: CFO says auditor could not validate full development capitalization by September and unmaterialised technology-transfer revenue was reversed. Management says products were commercialised and accounting methodologies did not change.
reconciliations.normalization: No automatic add-back. Expense is an economic product-development cost; revenue did not materialize.

reconciliations.subject: CFO classification
reconciliations.status: Mechanical reclassification available; broader historical residual not resolved
reconciliations.limitation: The FY25 noncash opening-reserve adjustment is embedded in reported CFO. An optimistic add-back of all 4.1679 crore is shown separately, not asserted as correct. Long-term contract advances remain additional cash deployment.

reconciliations.subject: Subsidiary effective date
reconciliations.company_early_statement: June call and introductory annual-report language call Swastik acquired in February. Board report says not subsidiary at March 31.
reconciliations.resolution: 25 September 2026 exchange filing establishes fresh subscription completion and subsidiary status on that date. Historical FY26 is correctly standalone; no allegation from absence of consolidation.

reconciliations.subject: Share count
reconciliations.status: Issuer allotment governs current economic shares
reconciliations.explanation: FY26 share note prints FY24 opening shares 9516138 plus issue3424000; FY25/prospectus and actual IPO are9516538 plus3423600. Both give12940138. Use exact allotment, not rounded table.

notes: The lost-advance sensitivity assumes a new cash payment to replace impaired productive contract advances. A write-off alone is noncash; the original advance is already paid and included in opening ONWC.
No ordinary return or entry while financial reliability and current group financeability remain unverified.
Hypothetical rescue is separately priced and funded net of fees; negative cash is a gap, not a new debt facility.

Cash-floor breaches before entry invalidate non-rescue conditional returns too. March-to-August operating cash is tested immediately before the actual 18 August capital receipt. Opening tax and statutory balances are conservatively assumed paid by then, not backfilled with later equity. This is a conditional timing assumption, not an actual cash/default finding.
No subsidy/DRDO ₹8.73 crore is assumed to be unrestricted cash. No IPO proceeds are added again.
No secondary acquisition payment assumed: Swastik subscription remains group cash until actually consumed, but is not assumed accessible to parent.

AS operating rents are in margin; no Ind AS lease asset/claim invented. Known gratuity/capital creditors/accrued interest counted once. Opening income tax ₹0.4569 crore and statutory liabilities ₹0.3545 crore are paid once before entry; future tax is modeled in CFO.
March debt assumes WC and related-party rollover unless stress states otherwise; this is a sensitivity, not proof of financeability.

liquidity.status: 60 of 60 issuer sessions verified. Framework starting score 9; explicit one-point downgrade to 8 for ST-series restrictions, large lot granularity and unobserved spread/queues.
